taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes mitochondrial clades do not follow subspecies boundaries and Crother (2017) tentatively retains three subspecies.
fieldMarks: Generally grayish-green back and yellow belly; pale (not white) stripes on the sides on the 2nd and 3rd scale rows above the belly scales.
Mid-dorsal stripe is bright and runs the full body length in some areas, dull and fading at midbody in others; dark spots sometimes on the back; melanistic forms occur.
Often two large blackish marks on the neck and irregular black marks on the belly.
Usually 8 upper labials on each side, keeled dorsal scales and usually 21 scale rows at midbody.
Total length to 109 cm, but few exceed 76 cm.
behavior: Diurnal: warms in the morning sun on heat-retaining surfaces, hunts through the day, and returns to shelter in the evening or in summer heat.
Solitary while active but dens communally in winter, usually returning to the same rocky hibernation site each year.

Coastal snakes mainly eat land prey (slugs, salamanders, small mammals, lizards); inland snakes hunt in and around water for frog and toad larvae, leeches and fish; hunts by movement and chemical cues.
When threatened it secretes a foul-smelling chemical from the cloaca and musk glands.
habitat: Often near lakes and slow streams but also in deserts, plains, mountains, meadows and forests, from sea level to about 3,990 m; hibernates in rocky areas.
range: Northern Mexico (Baja California) through the western United States, from New Mexico to western Oklahoma and Nebraska, the Dakotas and the Canadian border west to the Pacific Coast; in Canada, central and southern Saskatchewan, Alberta and Manitoba.

lookalikes.name: Common gartersnake (Thamnophis sirtalis)
lookalikes.howToTell: Common gartersnake has 7 upper labials, 19 scale rows at midbody and a uniformly dark head; terrestrial usually has 8 upper labials and 21 rows.

lookalikes.name: Aquatic gartersnake (Thamnophis atratus)
lookalikes.howToTell: Separate species (Rossman and Stewart 1987); the aquatic gartersnake is the stream-bound Pacific Coast snake.
